scope: factorized complete N2LO W1 projection performance; scalar driver measurements are single-thread and production measurements record their effective OpenMP count

openmp_scaling_after_P123_thread_restore.pre_fix_explanation: P123_omp_num_threads leaked into subsequent OpenMP regions, so requested OMP_NUM_THREADS values from 8 through 96 all executed W1 with three threads.

momentum_independent_warmup_ablation.reason: Removing the discarded warm-up call helps one thread slightly but creates concurrent first-use cache contention and is 52.6 percent slower at 16 threads and 76.2 percent slower at 96 threads.

metadata_only_warmup.status: accepted as a redundant-work removal, not a claimed wall-time speedup
metadata_only_warmup.interpretation: The one- and 16-thread points improve slightly while the 96-thread point regresses within observed run-to-run variation; no material speedup is claimed.

generic_order2_artifact_example.description: Raw constant-kernel scalar PWD for a spectator-D LS channel that is exactly zero

analytic_cE_contact.U_change_interpretation: The old transfer-order-two run contained nonzero contact leakage in higher orbital channels. The change is an intentional low-order quadrature correction, not a physical Ay result.

cD_cost_probe_before_analytic_x_reductio.interpretation: At transfer order two the cD path contributes about 10 percent of single-thread W1 wall time and is not the dominant remaining cost.

analytic_cD_relative_angle.identity: Integral[-1,1] P_lbar(x) dx = 2 delta_lbar,0 because the cD scalar propagator is independent of the relative transfer angle
analytic_cD_relative_angle.interpretation: The values are numerically unchanged and the timing shift is within run variation at transfer order two. The remaining cost is dominated by the angle-dependent c1/c3/c4 two-pion kernels.

changes: accumulate c1 and c3 reduced radial kernels in one pass when both LECs are active
precompute the four external-momentum bases at powers zero through four once per Cartesian projection
replace the ordered magnetic-orbital cache with a hashed cache
serve immutable Cartesian weight tables from a thread-local read cache after first use
two_pion_projection_hot_path.interpretation: The speedup comes from eliminating repeated transcendental evaluation, ordered-tree lookup, and shared-mutex traffic in the c4-dominated projection loop. The operator formula, quadrature nodes, and per-component accumulation order are unchanged.

changes: evaluate the common regulator and Fourier normalization once per momentum tuple instead of once per channel
serve immutable LS expansions and transfer quadrature grids from thread-local front caches
memoize the four channel-only isospin matrix elements per LS-channel pair

verification.CPP_make: passed with the documented conda HDF5/LAPACK prefix

batch_invariant_reuse.interpretation: The removed work is invariant across the channel batch or depends only on discrete channel metadata. Cached W1 doubles and downstream outputs are bitwise unchanged.

verification.hermitian_reuse_explanation: Reverse slabs are now exact transposes instead of separately accumulated quadrature results.

correctness_after_optimization.hermitian_transpose_layout: all p/q index permutations passed on a two-bin-per-axis cache test

notes: Timings use /usr/bin/time around a fresh driver process.
The complete pass enumerates alpha 0..9 and alpha 10..19 separately, preserving parity selection.
The angular-cache, magnetic-factorization, and channel-batching optimizations do not alter the operator formula or per-element summation order.
Exact-Hermitian reuse deliberately replaces separately accumulated reverse slabs with exact transposes; W1 cache schema v7 prevents mixing the two construction contracts.
Before commit 2563e8c, the P123-specific thread limit remained active for W1 and the solver. Restoring the caller setting exposes real W1 scaling without changing P123's requested thread count.
Commits 9eaa5f8 and 964d4d7 remove projection hot-path and batch-invariant overhead without changing cached W1 values, so the W1 cache schema remains v9.
